event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War refers to the 2026 international armed conflict centered on Iran, the United States and Israel, with effects extending across the Persian Gulf and neighboring states. U.S. combat operations began on February 28, 2026; the conflict has also made security and commercial navigation in the Strait of Hormuz a central issue.

facts.label: Start date
facts.value: The United States notified the UN Security Council that it commenced combat operations against Iran on February 28, 2026; U.S. energy officials likewise identify military action on that date as the point after which Hormuz traffic was effectively disrupted.

facts.label: Principal parties and stated U.S. purpos
facts.value: In its UN notification, the United States said it was acting in cooperation with Israel, citing protection of U.S. forces and regional partners and the free flow of maritime commerce through the Strait of Hormuz. These are the U.S. government's stated objectives, not an independent legal finding.

facts.label: Legal position asserted by the United St
facts.value: The United States characterized its operations as necessary and proportionate self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter, including collective self-defense of Israel.

facts.label: Why the Strait of Hormuz matters
facts.value: The strait lies between Iran and Oman and links the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. In the first half of 2025, about 20.9 million barrels per day of oil—roughly one-fifth of global petroleum-liquids consumption—moved through it, while alternative routes could replace only part of disrupted flows.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers chosen developments on July 22-23, 2026—including military threats, U.S. war-powers action and oil-market effects—and does not attempt to provide a complete account of the conflict, diplomacy, or humanitarian consequences.

facts.label: Prevention and public safety
facts.value: France treats forest and vegetation fires as a major natural-risk issue and uses prevention planning, vegetation-clearing obligations in designated risk areas, public alerts and civil-protection guidance. event_overview.title: About Ukraine Conflict
event_overview.subject: Ukraine Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Ukraine conflict is an armed conflict that began with Russia’s 2014 seizure of Crimea and fighting in eastern Ukraine, then expanded into a full-scale Russian armed attack across Ukraine on 24 February 2022. It includes frontline combat, long-range missile and drone strikes, attacks affecting civilian infrastructure, displacement, and international legal and diplomatic efforts to end the war and establish accountability.

facts.label: Conflict timeline
facts.value: The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine has operated since 2014; it identifies 24 February 2022 as the start of the Russian Federation’s full-scale armed attack, after which it focused on the international armed conflict’s human-rights impact.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: The war affects territory across Ukraine, including areas near the frontline, cities far from it, and territory occupied by the Russian Federation; Kyiv is among the urban centres affected by long-range attacks.

facts.label: Civilian-harm pattern
facts.value: UN monitors reported that long-range weapons, including missiles and drones, were the leading cause of civilian casualties in June 2026, with many casualties occurring in urban areas far from the frontline; short-range drones were a major danger in frontline areas.

facts.label: International position
facts.value: On 2 March 2022, the UN General Assembly adopted resolution ES-11/1, deploring Russia’s aggression against Ukraine and demanding that Russia end its use of force and withdraw its military forces.

facts.label: International Court of Justice proceedin
facts.value: In provisional measures ordered on 16 March 2022 in Ukraine v. Russian Federation, the International Court of Justice directed Russia to suspend the military operations it commenced on 24 February 2022, while stating that the order did not decide jurisdiction or the merits of the case.

event_overview.scope_note: This Muninn timeline follows selected conflict developments, including the specified strike near Kyiv, rather than providing a complete record of military operations, civilian harm, diplomacy, or legal proceedings.

facts.label: Seismic-intensity system

event_overview.title: About Iran Conflict
event_overview.subject: Iran Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Iran Conflict refers here to the 2026 direct military confrontation between the United States and Iran, which has expanded beyond Iranian territory to include attacks and claimed attacks on U.S. forces, partner states and maritime activity in the Middle East. The confrontation has centered in part on control and security of the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran’s reported retaliatory operations have involved missiles and drones directed at regional sites hosting U.S. personnel.

facts.label: Start of the direct conflict
facts.value: Reporting describes U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28, 2026, as the start of the present direct war; it is distinct from the longer-running U.S.-Iran rivalry and regional proxy conflicts.

facts.label: Ceasefire and renewed fighting
facts.value: The United States and Iran reached an interim arrangement or ceasefire in mid-June 2026, but reporting says the truce subsequently broke down amid a confrontation over the Strait of Hormuz and renewed U.S. and Iranian attacks.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: The conflict’s military and economic effects extend across Iran, the Strait of Hormuz and neighboring states that host U.S. facilities, including Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan; reports of individual strikes and damage may be contested or unverified.

facts.label: Why Bahrain and Kuwait matter
facts.value: Bahrain hosts U.S. Naval Support Activity Bahrain and the U.S. Fifth Fleet/NAVCENT presence, while Camp Arifjan in Kuwait supports Army prepositioned stocks and theater sustainment for U.S. Central Command operations.

facts.label: Maritime dimension
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz is a central theater because it is a strategic shipping chokepoint; the U.S. Fifth Fleet’s area of responsibility includes the Arabian Gulf and the strait, alongside other regional waterways.

event_overview.title: About Youth Protests
event_overview.subject: Youth Protests
event_overview.summary: Youth-led demonstrations in India grew around alleged irregularities in the 2026 National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test for undergraduate medical education (NEET-UG), including claims of a leaked paper and the disruption caused by a nationwide re-examination. The protests, centered visibly in New Delhi but supported more broadly, expanded into demands for accountability, examination-system reforms, and the education minister’s departure.

facts.label: Examination and re-test dates
facts.value: NTA scheduled NEET-UG 2026 for May 3, 2026; its official notices show that a re-examination was conducted on June 21, 2026.

facts.label: Examination purpose
facts.value: NEET-UG is the common, uniform entrance test for undergraduate medical education in India; it also applies to specified undergraduate Indian-system-of-medicine and homeopathy courses.

facts.label: Exam administrator
facts.value: The National Testing Agency (NTA), an autonomous organization under India’s Ministry of Education’s Department of Higher Education, administers NEET-UG and other national entrance examinations.

facts.label: Protest setting and stated demands
facts.value: The movement’s most visible sit-in site was Jantar Mantar in central New Delhi. Organizers sought the education minister’s resignation, examination reforms, and compensation for families of students reported to have died by suicide after exam irregularities.

facts.label: Legal context
facts.value: India’s Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, in force from June 21, 2024, covers paper or answer-key leaks and related collusion among prohibited unfair means in covered public examinations.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline focuses on the youth mobilization and ministerial-resignation developments of July 25, 2026, rather than providing a complete account of the NEET investigation, re-examination administration, court process, or all related education-policy disputes.

event_overview.title: About Israeli-Palestinian Conflict
event_overview.subject: Israeli-Palestinian Conflict
event_overview.summary: This is a localized deadly episode in the West Bank within the broader Israeli-Palestinian conflict, involving Palestinians, Israeli settlers and Israeli security authorities. Such incidents occur amid unresolved disputes over territory, security, settlements, Palestinian self-determination and the status of Jerusalem.

facts.label: Modern conflict timeline
facts.value: The question of Palestine was brought to the United Nations in 1947; the UN proposed partition that year, Israel declared independence on 14 May 1948, and Israel occupied the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and Gaza during the June 1967 war.

facts.label: Location and territorial framework
facts.value: The West Bank, including East Jerusalem, is central to the conflict. In its 19 July 2024 advisory opinion, the International Court of Justice described the Palestinian territory occupied since 1967 as encompassing the West Bank, East Jerusalem and the Gaza Strip, treated as a single territorial unit for the opinion’s legal analysis.

facts.label: Political parties and interim governance
facts.value: Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization signed the 13 September 1993 Declaration of Principles, which envisioned a Palestinian interim self-government authority in the West Bank and Gaza and negotiations on permanent-status issues including Jerusalem, refugees, settlements, security and borders.

facts.label: Settlements and international diplomacy
facts.value: UN Security Council resolution 2334 (2016) states that Israeli settlement activity in the Palestinian territory occupied since 1967, including East Jerusalem, has no legal validity and is a major obstacle to a two-state solution; the resolution calls for settlement activity to cease.

event_overview.summary: The Berlin Pride attack refers to a deadly assault in the Tiergarten area of central Berlin on July 25, 2026, during the city’s Christopher Street Day (CSD) weekend. facts.label: Date and location
facts.value: Authorities place the attack at about 10 p.m. on July 25, 2026, in the Tiergarten area of Berlin, in the vicinity of Christopher Street Day celebrations.

facts.label: Alleged method and casualties
facts.value: The Berlin General Prosecutor’s Office said the suspect was alleged to have injured several people with a rented vehicle and a bladed weapon; a woman died that evening and other people were seriously injured.

facts.label: Underlying event
facts.value: Berlin CSD 2026 was the 48th Berlin Christopher Street Day, organized by Berliner CSD e.V.; organizers described it as a demonstration for democracy, diversity and human rights.

facts.label: CSD schedule and format
facts.value: The Pride weekend was scheduled for July 24-25, 2026. Its July 25 demonstration was to begin on Leipziger Straße, proceed via Potsdamer Platz and Nollendorfplatz toward the Victory Column, with programming around the Brandenburg Gate.

facts.label: Investigation
facts.value: The Berlin General Prosecutor’s Office and police described the case as an active investigation and said that detailed public disclosures were limited in order to protect it.

event_overview.summary: The Iran War is the 2026 armed conflict involving U.S. and Israeli military operations against Iran and Iranian retaliatory attacks on U.S. and regional targets. It began with large-scale strikes on February 28, 2026, expanded into a regional security and maritime crisis, and has continued despite ceasefire and diplomatic efforts.

facts.label: Start and parties
facts.value: The current conflict began on February 28, 2026, when the United States and Israel carried out major strikes in Iran; Iran subsequently announced attacks on U.S. military assets in the region.

facts.label: U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says it commenced Operation Epic Fury at the President's direction at 1:15 a.m. on February 28, 2026, describing its stated aim as dismantling Iran's security apparatus and prioritizing locations it considers imminent threats.

facts.label: Regional scope
facts.value: The conflict has affected Iran and neighboring states across the Gulf and Middle East; the UN reported Iranian attacks or reported impacts involving Bahrain, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

facts.label: Strait of Hormuz and shipping
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz has become a central theater because it is a strategically important Gulf shipping route. CENTCOM said it began blocking maritime traffic entering and leaving Iranian ports on April 13, while the UN has warned that maritime incidents and threats to navigation heighten escalation risks.

facts.label: Diplomacy and legal context
facts.value: The UN has urged de-escalation, respect for the UN Charter and international humanitarian law. It reported that Qatar-mediated talks sought to implement a June 17 memorandum of understanding, but renewed strikes and counterstrikes underscored the fragility of those arrangements.

event_overview.subject: Brazil Elections
event_overview.summary: Brazil’s 2026 general elections will choose the country’s president and vice president alongside governors, senators, and federal and state or district legislators. The presidential contest is a nationwide direct election administered by Brazil’s Electoral Justice, with a second round if no ticket wins an absolute majority of valid votes in the first round.

facts.label: Election dates
facts.value: The first round is scheduled for October 4, 2026; a second round, where required, is scheduled for October 25, 2026.

facts.label: Offices being elected
facts.value: Voters will elect the president and vice president, state and Federal District governors and vice governors, senators, federal deputies, and state or district deputies; two Senate seats are being contested in each state and the Federal District in this cycle.

facts.label: Electoral system for president
facts.value: The president and vice president run as a single ticket. A ticket must receive an absolute majority of valid votes to win in the first round; otherwise, the two leading tickets proceed to a runoff.

facts.label: Candidate selection and registration
facts.value: Political parties and federations may hold conventions from July 20 through August 5, 2026 to choose candidates and decide coalitions. A public campaign launch is distinct from the formal registration process; presidential and vice-presidential registration requests are decided by the Superior Electoral Court (TSE).

facts.label: Election administration
facts.value: The Superior Electoral Court’s 2026 rules govern preparation, voting, vote counting, tabulation, certification of winners, and post-election procedures for the general election.

event_overview.subject: Tate Brothers Arrest
event_overview.summary: The event concerns the July 2026 U.S. arrest of Andrew and Tristan Tate after UK prosecutors sought their extradition to face criminal charges in England. It is an extradition and charging matter, not a finding of guilt: the Crown Prosecution Service says the proceedings are active and that guilt can be determined only by a court.

facts.label: Arrest and location
facts.value: The brothers were arrested by the U.S. Marshals Service in the United States on July 18, 2026; reporting and the selected timeline identify Miami, Florida, as the location of the arrest.

facts.label: UK charging scope
facts.value: The CPS said it would pursue extradition on 21 pre-existing charges and further charges involving four additional alleged victims. The added allegations include rape, arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, assault, and offences relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.

facts.label: Alleged time period and victims
facts.value: According to the CPS, the further alleged offending occurred between July 2010 and August 2017; the charging decisions brought the stated total number of alleged victims in the UK case to seven.

facts.label: Earlier extradition history
facts.value: UK extradition warrants were issued at Westminster Magistrates’ Court in January 2024. In March 2024, the Bucharest Court of Appeal ordered extradition to the UK only after separate Romanian criminal proceedings concluded.

facts.label: Legal status
facts.value: The CPS requested extradition from the United States, and as of July 19, 2026 said the brothers had been arrested and were awaiting extradition proceedings. The CPS emphasizes that a charging decision is not a finding of fact or guilt and that the defendants have a right to a fair trial.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the Miami arrest and the initial U.S. extradition challenge from July 19–21, 2026, rather than the underlying evidence, the separate Romanian proceedings, or any eventual extradition or trial outcome.

event_overview.title: About US-Saudi Nuclear Deal
event_overview.subject: US-Saudi Nuclear Deal
event_overview.summary: The event concerns a U.S.-Saudi agreement for peaceful nuclear cooperation, commonly called a “123 agreement,” signed on July 22, 2026 alongside a bilateral safeguards agreement. It establishes a legal framework for potential U.S. civil-nuclear exports and commercial participation in Saudi Arabia’s nuclear-energy program, while making nonproliferation, safety and security central stated objectives.

facts.label: Parties and date
facts.value: U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright and Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman signed the peaceful nuclear cooperation agreement and an accompanying bilateral safeguards agreement on July 22, 2026.

facts.label: Legal framework
facts.value: The accord is a Section 123 agreement under the U.S. Atomic Energy Act of 1954—the mechanism used for significant civil nuclear cooperation, including NRC-licensed exports of nuclear material, reactors, equipment and components.

facts.label: Congressional process
facts.value: The Department of Energy said the agreement would be transmitted to Congress for review; standard Section 123 agreements are subject to two review periods totaling 90 days of continuous congressional session before they may enter into force absent enacted disapproval.

facts.label: Stated purpose
facts.value: DOE describes the arrangement as supporting U.S. access to Saudi nuclear-energy opportunities and Saudi energy needs, while advancing nuclear safety, security and nonproliferation objectives.

facts.label: International safeguards context
facts.value: Saudi Arabia’s comprehensive safeguards agreement with the International Atomic Energy Agency has been in force since January 13, 2009; its Small Quantities Protocol was rescinded effective December 31, 2024.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the July 22–23, 2026 approval/signing and finalization developments, not the subsequent congressional review, implementation, specific export licenses, commercial contracts, or construction of any Saudi nuclear facilities.

event_overview.subject: Tropical Storms
event_overview.summary: This tracked event concerns concurrent tropical cyclones affecting two U.S. National Hurricane Center monitoring areas: Bertha in the Atlantic basin, including the Gulf Coast, and Fausto in the eastern North Pacific. Tropical storms are named tropical cyclones with sustained winds of 39–73 mph; once sustained winds reach 74 mph, they are classified as hurricanes.

facts.label: Seasonal timing
facts.value: The Atlantic hurricane season, which includes the Gulf of America, officially runs from June 1 through November 30; the eastern Pacific season runs from May 15 through November 30.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: The eastern North Pacific basin is the portion of the North Pacific Ocean east of 140°W, while the Atlantic basin includes the Atlantic Ocean, Caribbean Sea, and Gulf of America.

facts.label: Storm classifications
facts.value: A tropical storm has maximum sustained winds of 39–73 mph; a hurricane has maximum sustained winds of at least 74 mph. Major hurricanes are Category 3–5 systems, beginning at 111 mph.

facts.label: Forecasting authority
facts.value: NOAA’s National Hurricane Center in Miami is responsible for tracking tropical cyclones in both the Atlantic and eastern North Pacific and issues operational products including forecasts, public advisories, discussions, and wind-probability information for active cyclones.

facts.label: Naming system
facts.value: Bertha is on the 2026 Atlantic storm-name list. Tropical-cyclone names are assigned from rotating lists maintained through the World Meteorological Organization system.

event_overview.title: About Netanyahu Arrest Warrant
event_overview.subject: Netanyahu Arrest Warrant
event_overview.summary: The Netanyahu arrest-warrant event concerns an International Criminal Court (ICC) warrant issued for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the Court’s Situation in the State of Palestine. The warrant has become a focus of debate over the ICC’s jurisdiction, the alleged crimes identified by the Court, and whether national or local authorities can or must act if Netanyahu travels abroad.

facts.label: Warrant date and court
facts.value: ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I issued an arrest warrant for Benjamin Netanyahu on November 21, 2024, in the ICC’s Situation in the State of Palestine.

facts.label: Allegations at the warrant stage
facts.value: The Chamber found reasonable grounds to believe Netanyahu was responsible for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity, including starvation as a method of warfare, murder, persecution, and other inhumane acts. These are allegations supporting a warrant, not a conviction.

facts.label: Underlying investigation
facts.value: The ICC Prosecutor opened the Situation in Palestine investigation on March 3, 2021; it covers alleged Rome Statute crimes committed since June 13, 2014. The Court had held that its territorial jurisdiction for this situation extends to Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem.

facts.label: Jurisdiction dispute
facts.value: On November 21, 2024, the same ICC chamber rejected Israel’s then-pending jurisdiction and notification challenges, stating that Israel’s acceptance was not required for the Court to exercise territorial jurisdiction based on Palestine and that the jurisdiction challenge was premature at that stage.

facts.label: Enforcement framework
facts.value: The ICC does not itself carry out arrests; arrest powers rest with states. States Parties to the Rome Statute have obligations to cooperate with ICC arrest-and-surrender requests, while the United States is not a party to the Rome Statute.

event_overview.scope_note: This Muninn timeline follows New York City political and legal statements in July 2026 about possible action on the ICC warrant; it does not attempt to chronicle the full ICC case, the Gaza war, or all international responses to the warrant.

event_overview.title: About Cockroach Movement Protests
event_overview.subject: Cockroach Movement Protests
event_overview.summary: The Cockroach Movement is a youth-led Indian protest movement organized around the self-styled Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). It began as online satire in May 2026 and developed into street protests focused on alleged examination irregularities, education reform, unemployment and government accountability; supporters have specifically called for the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

facts.label: Origins and status
facts.value: The CJP emerged online in May 2026 and had become an active, ongoing protest movement by July 21, 2026 rather than a formally established political party or a time-limited event.

facts.label: First major street action
facts.value: Its first reported public street demonstration took place in New Delhi on June 6, 2026, moving the campaign from social media into in-person protest.

facts.label: Organization and participants
facts.value: The movement is associated with the Cockroach Janta Party and its founder, Abhijeet Dipke; it is chiefly youth- and student-led, while later protests also drew professionals and families.

facts.label: Stated aims
facts.value: Its central demands concern accountability for alleged failures in India’s examination system and education reform, including a demand that the education minister resign; the movement also frames unemployment and broader government accountability as concerns.

facts.label: Examination context
facts.value: The protests arose amid controversy over NEET (UG) 2026. The National Testing Agency officially conducted a re-examination on June 21, 2026 and issued fee-refund notices for candidates from the original May 3 examination.

event_overview.subject: World Cup 2026
event_overview.summary: The FIFA World Cup 2026 is the 23rd edition of FIFA’s men’s national-team football championship. It is the first World Cup jointly hosted by Canada, Mexico and the United States, and its expanded field and knockout structure culminate in a final on July 19, 2026.

facts.label: Dates
facts.value: The tournament runs from June 11 through July 19, 2026.

facts.label: Hosts and venues
facts.value: Canada, Mexico and the United States are co-hosting the competition across 16 host cities; this is the first World Cup shared among three countries.

facts.label: Organizer and participants
facts.value: FIFA organizes the tournament, which has a record 48 participating national teams and 104 matches.

facts.label: Competition format
facts.value: The 48 teams are divided into 12 groups of four. The top two in each group and the eight best third-place teams advance to a Round of 32, followed by single-elimination rounds, including a third-place match and final.

facts.label: Concluding matches
facts.value: The third-place match is scheduled for July 18 at Miami Stadium, and the final is scheduled for July 19 at New York New Jersey Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
